evals.prompt: evals/files/spec.md の仕様をレビューして
evals.expected_output: A review that leads with the findings ordered by impact, each traced to sections of the spec and put as a question the author can answer, then the coverage (which models were written and which were left out) and the models as an appendix, with the cells the spec does not settle left marked rather than filled in.
expectations: Points out that 決済処理中 appears in §5 but not among the states in §3.2, and that what happens to it when 30 minutes pass or the user cancels is undefined
Points out that a payment completion notice arriving after the tentative reservation has expired leaves a charge with no slot, or two reservations on one slot
Points out that §3.1 (at most 2 reservations a day) and §6 (up to 5 group reservations a day) cannot both hold as written, or asks how they combine
Points out that §7 lets facility staff register a closure, which cancels and refunds reservations, while the role table in §4 does not give staff that operation
Points out that §8 promotes from the waiting list only on cancellation, leaving open what happens when a slot is freed by expiry or by a closure

Points out at least one state with no way out or an event with no defined result: a paid reservation nobody shows up for, a waiting-list entry that never gets a slot, or cancelling a waiting-list entry
Points out that 「前日まで」 (§3.4, §9) does not say until what time
Points out that 「すぐに」 in §11 comes with no numbers (expected load or response time)
Every finding names the section or sections of the spec it rests on
Findings are put as questions the author can answer, not only as fixes
The state table (or another model) leaves the cells the spec does not settle, such as (決済処理中, cancel), marked as unknown or implied, rather than filling them with a plausible behavior
Says which models were written and which were considered and left out, with a reason for each one left out
Every model the coverage says was written appears in the appendix, including any that found nothing; anything only glanced at is described as such rather than counted as written
Ends by offering to write a checklist of what to confirm, without writing the checklist unasked
Says the checks are a careful reading, not a proof
Does not report the wordy sentence in §1 as a defect

evals.prompt: evals/files/spec.md（仕様）と evals/files/design.md（設計）をレビューして
evals.expected_output: A review that models the spec and the design and compares them, reporting where the design does not carry out the spec and where the design itself breaks under concurrency or failure, each traced to sections of both documents.
expectations: Points out that design §4.1 checks for a free slot with SELECT and then INSERTs, with only an application check in §2, so two requests at once (most likely at 9:00, spec §9 and §11) can both get the slot
Points out that a promoted reservation keeps the created_at of its waiting-list entry, so the 30-minute expiry in design §4.2 can cancel it at once, against spec §8's 30 minutes from the notice
Points out that the status enum in design §2 has no 決済処理中 and that design §4.5 sets paid on any notice, so a late notice can turn an expired or cancelled reservation into paid
Points out that no API in design §3 performs the attendance check, so used cannot be reached, or that no API is given to administrators
Points out that the design does not check that facility staff act only on their own facility (「担当施設」 in spec §4)
Points out that design §4.4 refunds one reservation after another inside the request, so a failure partway leaves some reservations cancelled or refunded and a retry may refund twice
Points out that the limits in spec §3.1 and §6 (2 a day, 5 group reservations, 20 members) are enforced nowhere in the design
Points out that the payment webhook has no check of who sent it, or no handling of a duplicate notice
Compares the spec's operations or permissions with the design's API in a table or list, so the missing ones are visible
Findings that involve both documents cite sections in both
Every model the coverage says was written appears in the appendix, including any that found nothing; anything only glanced at is described as such rather than counted as written
Ends by offering to write a checklist of what to confirm, without writing the checklist unasked
Says the checks are a careful reading, not a proof

evals.prompt: evals/files/spec.md の仕様をレビューして。確認項目のチェックリストも出して
evals.expected_output: The review, then a checklist grouped by model, each item a statement that can be confirmed against the built system with the section it comes from, and the cells the spec leaves open listed as waiting on an answer with the finding they wait on rather than as items.
expectations: Gives a checklist of Markdown `- [ ]` items grouped by model
Each item names the section of the spec it comes from

Includes items for cells the spec settles, for example that a tentative reservation not paid within 30 minutes expires and frees its slot (§3.3), or that cancelling a paid reservation by the day before refunds it in full (§3.4)
Does not turn an open cell into an item: no item says what happens to 決済処理中 after 30 minutes, what cancelling a waiting-list entry does, or whether group reservations count toward the daily limit
Lists the open cells as waiting on an answer, each with the finding it waits on and without a checkbox
Puts 「すぐに予約できる」 (§11) under waiting on an answer rather than as an item, since it has no number to confirm
Payment, refund and email failures appear only as waiting on an answer, not as items

evals.prompt: evals/files/design.md の設計書をレビューして
evals.expected_output: A review of the design on its own that models how it is built as well as what it does: the parts in its structure, which part writes which data, and the contract of each API, reporting the parts the structure leaves out, the data several parts write without coordination, and the calls whose errors, retries or callers are not settled, each traced to sections of the design and put as a question the author can answer.
expectations: Points out that the job in §4.2 that runs every five minutes appears nowhere in the structure in §1, so where it runs, and how many copies of it run, is unstated

Shows, in a CRUD matrix or a list of writers, that reservations.status is changed by §4.1, §4.2, §4.3, §4.4 and §4.5 with nothing putting the writes in order, and names at least one race that follows, such as a payment notice (§4.5) marking paid a reservation the job in §4.2 has just cancelled, or a cancellation and a closure both refunding the same reservation
Points out that the webhook in §3 and §4.5 does not check who sent it, or says nothing about a notice that arrives twice
Points out that the API in §3 names no errors, or that it is unstated whether retrying a call such as POST /reservations/{id}/payment or DELETE /reservations/{id} is safe
Points out data that nothing writes or nothing removes: nothing sets `used`, group members can be added but not removed, or nothing says how long reservations are kept
Points out that the calls to the payment and mail services in §4.3 and §4.4 have no stated behavior when they fail or time out
Says that the spec the design refers to (仕様書 v0.9) was not given, and keeps findings that would need it as questions or stated assumptions rather than facts
Writes the structure and the data ownership (which part writes which data) as models, and both appear in the appendix
Every finding names the section or sections of the design it rests on
Findings are put as questions the author can answer, not only as fixes
Says which models were written and which were considered and left out, with a reason for each one left out
Ends by offering to write a checklist of what to confirm, without writing the checklist unasked
Says the checks are a careful reading, not a proof
Does not report the lack of a C4 diagram, an architecture decision record or any other kind of document as a defect

evals.prompt: evals/files/architecture.md の設計書をレビューして
evals.expected_output: A review that models the structure of the split, which service writes which data, the contract of each API and message, and the migration with the combinations of old and new that meet during it, reporting what no service owns, the data with more than one writer, the calls that cannot be retried safely, and the steps of the migration that lose or strand data, each traced to sections of the document and put as a question the author can answer.
expectations: Points out that the overdue notice the next morning (§2) belongs to no service in §3: 通知サービス only sends mail it is asked to send, and nothing detects overdue loans

Points out that 会員サービス writes loans.status directly in the loans DB on withdrawal (§5.3), so loans has a second writer reaching into another service's store, with nothing putting it in order against a return or a loan at the same moment
Points out that marking loans `returned` on withdrawal while the books are still out (§5.3) makes the books look available, or loses track of books not yet collected
Points out that the search index is rebuilt once a night (§4.3), so the 貸出可 or 貸出中 shown in search (§2) can be up to a day out of date, or that 検索サービス reads the loans DB directly
Points out the synchronous cycle in §5.1 (貸出サービス → 会員サービス → 貸出サービス), or that lending stops whenever 会員サービス is down, with no timeout stated between the services
Points out that the terminal resends POST /loans after five seconds (§5.1) while nothing makes the call safe to repeat, so one copy can be recorded as lent twice
Points out that the queue delivers `loan.created` at least once (§5.4) while 通知サービス does not ignore repeats, so a member can get the same mail twice

Points out that the API in §6 names no errors beyond 400 and 500, so the terminal cannot tell a member over the limit from a withdrawn member or a failure, or that nothing says POST /loans/{id}/extend checks that the loan belongs to the member calling it
Points out that members.email is required (§4.2) while §2 lets a member register only a phone number, so existing members without an email cannot be copied as described in §7, or cannot be notified

Points out that during the week of step 3 (§7) the old system and the new services both take loans, from old terminals and from new terminals and the Web, against §7's statement that they are never written at once, so loans made in the old system after the copy in step 2 are lost, or a member can borrow up to the limit in each

Points out that a book lent on an old terminal and returned at another library on a new terminal (returns at any library, §2) cannot be found in the new loans DB, or names another combination of old and new that breaks
Points out that putting a terminal back to the old version (§7) leaves the loans it made on the new version out of the old system, or that going back once the new side has taken writes is unstated
Writes the structure, the data ownership (a CRUD matrix or equivalent), the interface contracts, and the migration with a table of the old and new combinations, and all of them appear in the appendix
Leaves the cells the document does not settle marked as unknown or implied, rather than filled with a plausible behavior
Every finding names the section or sections of the document it rests on
Findings are put as questions the author can answer, not only as fixes
Says which models were written and which were considered and left out, with a reason for each one left out
Ends by offering to write a checklist of what to confirm, without writing the checklist unasked
Says the checks are a careful reading, not a proof
Does not report the lack of a C4 diagram, an architecture decision record or a sequence diagram as a defect
